findings.title: Non-deterministic hash() used for shared cache key
findings.body: cache_key uses hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's hash() is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so different API workers generate different keys for the same projects in a shared Redis/memcached cache. Caching becomes ineffective and invalidate_upsampling_cache() cannot delete keys created by another worker, leaving stale entries.

findings.title: 60s eligibility cache returns stale allowlist decisions
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches _are_all_projects_error_upsampled for 60s and invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called on allowlist change. A project added/removed from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist will get wrong counts (upsampled 10x vs true count) for up to 60s. Tests in test_organization_events_stats.py mock different allowlists with same org/project_ids without clearing cache, so they pollute each other.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset which can differ from the outer dataset when dashboard-split logic retries with discover vs scoped_dataset, but eligibility is checked with the outer dataset variable. A discover split query for errors evaluated against a metrics/transactions dataset will never upsample, and vice versa.

findings.title: Error-focus check reads request.GET instead of executed query
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query inspects request.GET.get('query') while _get_event_stats executes a potentially rewritten query argument (e.g. errors_only_query='(query) AND !event.type:transaction' or transactions_only_query). Split queries therefore get the wrong upsampling decision. Empty discover queries also default to False even when the executed query is error-only.

findings.title: upsampled_count defined only for discover but applied to errors dataset
findings.body: _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True for dataset == errors unconditionally, then organization_events_stats rewrites count() to upsampled_count(). upsampled_count is only registered in discover.py function_converter, so errors-dataset timeseries/top-events queries will fail to resolve the function or hit a missing sample_weight column in Snuba.

findings.title: sum(sample_weight) without null handling and truncating cast
findings.body: upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with comment assuming the column always exists. Events without sample_weight (old rows, unsampled relays, transactions mixed in) make sum NULL/0 and undercount, and toInt64 truncates fractional weights (e.g. 1/0.33). Counts can silently drop to zero or lose precision instead of falling back to count.

findings.title: Only bare count() is rewritten
findings.body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only matches column_lower == 'count()'. Common variants like 'count() as count', 'count_if(...)', 'count_unique(...)' or equations pass through unchanged, so an allowlisted error query silently returns un-upsampled numbers while the caller assumes upsampling was applied.

findings.title: Internal upsampled_count exposed as public function
findings.body: The neighboring count() SnQLFunction is declared private=True, but the new upsampled_count omits private, making it callable directly via Discover search. Users can bypass the allowlist gate and get incorrect sums on projects without sample_weight.

findings.title: Test factory silently overwrites sample_rate
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling unconditionally sets normalized_data['sample_rate'] from contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate with bare except:pass and if client_sample_rate truthiness check. It overwrites any explicit sample_rate, accepts out-of-range values, and changes behavior for every store_event caller globally, not just upsampling tests.
